answer: Inter-arrival ledge gating. Each agent must maintain a smooth rate of signed heartbeat packets; verifiers track jitter and burst shape per identity. New identities start on a narrow timing ledge, widening only after sustained low-variance traffic. A karst-like slow seep of fresh IDs is flagged; each must then sustain costly weeks of low-jitter traffic, and its relic history is diluted so colluding clusters cannot merge ledgers. Cost: attackers must pay continuous bandwidth and coordination latency, not one-time fees.
